text: Which DAX function evaluates an expression in a modified filter context?

options.A: CALCULATE
options.B: FILTER
options.C: ALL
options.D: RELATED

explanation: CALCULATE is the only DAX function that can modify, overwrite, or add to the current filter context during evaluation.

text: What does SUMX do in Power BI?

options.A: Evaluates an expression for each row of a table and sums the results
options.B: Sums a single column of values directly
options.C: Sums values across multiple tables based on active relationships
options.D: Calculates the running total of a measure

explanation: SUMX is an iterator function that evaluates the specified expression for every row of a table, then sums the results.

text: Why would you use FILTER inside CALCULATE instead of a simple boolean filter?

options.A: To apply complex filter conditions involving measures or multiple columns
options.B: To speed up the query execution time significantly
options.C: To automatically clear all other active filters on the table
options.D: To change the cardinality of the underlying relationship

explanation: Simple boolean filters in CALCULATE have restrictions (e.g. cannot reference measures or columns from different tables). FILTER allows complex logic.

text: Which DAX function returns a related value from another table?

options.A: RELATED
options.B: LOOKUPVALUE
options.C: CALCULATE
options.D: USERELATIONSHIP

explanation: RELATED follows the active relationship from the many-side to the one-side to retrieve a corresponding value.

text: How does RANKX determine the rank if there is a tie in values?

options.A: Depending on the optional 'ties' parameter (Skip or Dense)
options.B: It always assigns the next sequential rank randomly
options.C: It averages the rank values of all tied rows
options.D: It throws a model evaluation runtime error

explanation: RANKX supports 'Skip' (leaves gaps in ranking) and 'Dense' (no gaps in ranking) parameters to handle ties.

text: Which schema structure is recommended as the best practice for Power BI data modeling?

options.A: Star Schema
options.B: Snowflake Schema
options.C: Flat Table Schema
options.D: Circular Dependent Schema

explanation: A Star Schema with distinct facts and dimensions is the optimal layout for Power BI usability, performance, and DAX simplicity.

text: What is the danger of using a Many-to-Many relationship direction in Power BI?

options.A: It can lead to ambiguous filter paths and unexpected data aggregation
options.B: It completely disables the use of DAX time intelligence functions
options.C: It limits the report to a maximum of 1,000 rows of data
options.D: It forces Power BI to convert all values into text

explanation: Many-to-many relationships introduce ambiguity in how filters propagate, which can lead to incorrect or misleading report numbers.

text: What is the default relationship cardinality when connecting a unique DimCustomer table to a FactSales table?

options.A: One-to-Many (1:*)
options.B: Many-to-One (*:1)
options.C: One-to-One (1:1)
options.D: Many-to-Many (*:*)

explanation: DimCustomer has unique IDs (One) and FactSales contains multiple transactions per customer (Many), creating a One-to-Many relationship.

text: Which setting controls how filters propagate between tables in a relationship?

options.A: Cross filter direction
options.B: Cardinality type
options.C: Active status
options.D: Security propagation

explanation: Cross filter direction (Single or Both) determines how filters flow from one table to another across relationships.

text: How can you resolve circular dependency relationships in Power BI?

options.A: Make one of the active relationships inactive and use USERELATIONSHIP in DAX
options.B: Merge all dimension tables into a single flat database view
options.C: Enable bidirectional cross-filtering on all relationships
options.D: Disable direct data modeling and perform calculations in Power Query only

explanation: Making relationships inactive removes the circular loop, and you can selectively activate them in measures using USERELATIONSHIP.

text: Where do you perform data cleaning and transformation tasks in Power BI Desktop?

options.A: Power Query Editor
options.B: Model View tab
options.C: Report Canvas settings
options.D: Service workspace options

explanation: Power Query Editor is the built-in ETL tool used to clean, shape, and transform data before loading it into the data model.

text: What is 'Query Folding' in Power Query?

options.A: Translating Power Query steps into a single SQL statement executed by the source database
options.B: Compressing multiple steps into a single combined M language function
options.C: Caching query outputs locally to speed up report rendering time
options.D: Grouping columns together inside the modeling interface

explanation: Query folding is the optimization where Power Query pushes transformations back to the source database as a single SQL query.

text: Which operation combines two tables by adding rows from one table to another?

options.A: Append Queries
options.B: Merge Queries
options.C: Group By
options.D: Pivot Columns

explanation: Append Queries stacks rows from one or more tables on top of each other, similar to a UNION operation in SQL.

text: Which operation is equivalent to a SQL JOIN in Power Query?

options.A: Merge Queries
options.B: Append Queries
options.C: Transpose
options.D: Unpivot Columns

explanation: Merge Queries joins two tables side-by-side based on matching key columns, just like a JOIN statement in SQL.

text: What language is used to write formulas and scripts in Power Query?

options.A: M formula language
options.B: DAX language
options.C: SQL queries
options.D: Python script

explanation: Power Query uses the M formula language (informally known as M) to define ETL steps and transformations.

text: Which visual is best suited to show relationships between two continuous variables?

options.A: Scatter chart
options.B: Stacked bar chart
options.C: Treemap
options.D: Card visual

explanation: Scatter charts plot pairs of numerical coordinates on both axes, making them ideal for correlation and relationship analysis.

text: When should you use a Treemap visual instead of a Bar chart?

options.A: To display hierarchical data with large numbers of categories in a nested layout
options.B: To compare two simple metrics side-by-side over a period of time
options.C: To plot geological coordinate data on a map interface
options.D: To show the correlation between two independent metrics

explanation: Treemaps use nested rectangles to represent hierarchies and values, making it easy to compare sizes across complex categories.

text: What is the purpose of the Key Influencers visual in Power BI?

options.A: To run machine learning analyses on factors driving a metric up or down
options.B: To track social media engagement metrics for influencer campaigns
options.C: To create organizational hierarchy trees automatically
options.D: To highlight high-performing cells in a matrix layout

explanation: The Key Influencers visual analyzes your data, ranks factors that affect your metric, and displays them as key influencers.

text: Which visual is best for showing composition of a category over time?

options.A: 100% stacked area chart
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Line chart
options.D: KPI visual

explanation: A 100% stacked area chart shows how the parts that make up a whole change over time, maintaining a total height of 100%.

text: What feature enables interactive filtering of other report elements by clicking a chart element?

options.A: Cross-filtering / Cross-highlighting
options.B: Tooltips
options.C: Bookmarks
options.D: Drillthrough

explanation: Clicking a data point in one visual automatically filters or highlights related data in other visuals through cross-filtering.

text: Where is Row-Level Security (RLS) defined in Power BI?

options.A: Power BI Desktop (roles/rules) and Power BI Service (assigning members)
options.B: Directly in the source SQL Database using security scripts
options.C: In the local computer registry of the report viewer
options.D: Inside the Power Query Editor M code parameters only

explanation: Roles and validation rules are configured in Power BI Desktop, but users are assigned to those roles inside the Power BI Service workspace.

text: Which DAX function is commonly used to dynamic filter data based on the logged-in user's email in RLS?

options.A: USERPRINCIPALNAME()
options.B: USERNAME()
options.C: LOOKUPVALUE()
options.D: CALCULATEDMEMBER()

explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns the user principal name (often the email address) of the currently authenticated user in the Power BI service.

text: How can you test RLS roles before publishing to the Power BI Service?

options.A: Use the 'View as' button in the Security ribbon of Power BI Desktop
options.B: Create a second dummy account and log in on a separate browser
options.C: Deploy the report to a temporary workspace and run manual queries
options.D: Temporarily change the values in the fact table to match the test role

explanation: The 'View as' feature in Power BI Desktop lets you simulate how the report will appear for specific roles or users.

text: What type of RLS uses table-based relationships to assign security dynamically without hardcoding roles?

options.A: Dynamic RLS
options.B: Static RLS
options.C: Active RLS
options.D: Direct RLS

explanation: Dynamic RLS uses a security table containing user emails and access rights, filtering the data dynamically using USERPRINCIPALNAME().

text: If a user has 'Admin' workspace permissions, how does Row-Level Security (RLS) affect them?

options.A: RLS is bypassed, and they can see all data
options.B: RLS is strictly enforced, and they only see allowed rows
options.C: The report fails to load for them due to authorization loop
options.D: They can only see the schema, not the underlying rows

explanation: Workspace roles like Admin, Member, or Contributor bypass RLS and can view all data. RLS only applies to users with Viewer access.

text: What is the primary way to share a report securely with external partners in Power BI?

options.A: Publish a Power BI App or share the report direct link to guest users
options.B: Email the original pbix file as an attachment
options.C: Export the report to PDF and host it on a public website
options.D: Host the report inside a personal Microsoft OneDrive folder

explanation: Power BI Apps and report sharing allow controlled access for external (B2B guest) users via Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

text: What must you configure to allow data refresh for reports using local on-premises databases?

options.A: On-premises data gateway
options.B: XMLA Endpoint access link
options.C: A VPN connection to the Power BI Cloud
options.D: Custom Power Query parameters

explanation: An on-premises data gateway acts as a bridge, providing quick and secure data transfer between local data and the Power BI service.

text: What is the difference between a Report and a Dashboard in the Power BI Service?

options.A: A report is from a single dataset; a dashboard is a single-page canvas pinning visuals from multiple reports
options.B: Reports are interactive, but dashboards are strictly static images
options.C: Dashboards can only be built in Desktop, while reports are built in Service
options.D: There is no difference; they are different names for the same asset

explanation: Reports are multi-page interactive explorations of a single dataset. Dashboards are single-page displays created only in the Service.

text: How do you protect reports from being modified by members with Contributor access?

options.A: Publish the content as a read-only Power BI App
options.B: Set the workspace type to Premium Capacity only
options.C: Change the workspace role of the members to Viewer
options.D: Encrypt the dataset file using a master password

explanation: Workspace Contributors can modify reports and datasets. Changing their role to Viewer restricts them to read-only access.

text: Which cloud capacity type is required to share reports with free license users in Power BI?

options.A: Premium Capacity (P or F SKU)
options.B: Pro Capacity
options.C: Shared Capacity
options.D: Personal Capacity

explanation: Reports hosted in Premium Capacity workspaces can be shared with and viewed by users who only hold a free Power BI license.

text: What is the primary benefit of configuring Incremental Refresh in Power BI?

options.A: Faster refreshes, lower resource consumption, and ability to load massive datasets
options.B: Automatically updates visuals instantly when source data changes
options.C: Allows the report to bypass Row-Level Security rules
options.D: Converts all date columns to the UTC timezone automatically

explanation: Incremental refresh only updates the partition containing new/modified data, reducing resource usage and execution time.

text: Which parameters are mandatory in Power Query to set up Incremental Refresh?

options.A: RangeStart and RangeEnd (DateTime type)
options.B: RefreshDate and TodayDate (Date type)
options.C: MinDate and MaxDate (Integer type)
options.D: StartDate and EndDate (Text type)

explanation: RangeStart and RangeEnd must be configured as case-sensitive DateTime parameters to filter the data partition in Power Query.

text: If incremental refresh is configured, where is the initial full load of historical data processed?

options.A: During the first scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service
options.B: Locally on the user's computer inside Power BI Desktop
options.C: Inside the data gateway configuration interface
options.D: During the query folding translation phase

explanation: Power BI Desktop only loads a small preview. The first full load of historical data occurs during the first refresh in the Service.

text: Which feature must the source database support for incremental refresh to be efficient?

options.A: Query Folding
options.B: Bidirectional filtering
options.C: Stored Procedures
options.D: JSON serialization

explanation: Query folding allows Power BI to push date filters to the source database, retrieving only the required rows for the partition.

text: Can you download a .pbix file from the Power BI Service after Incremental Refresh has run?

options.A: No, reports using incremental refresh cannot be downloaded back to desktop
options.B: Yes, but only if the file size is under 50 MB
options.C: Yes, it downloads with all data intact
options.D: Yes, but the historical data partitions are stripped out

explanation: Once a dataset is modified by incremental refresh in the Service, it cannot be downloaded back as a .pbix file.

text: What is a Power BI Dataflow?

options.A: A reusable self-service data prep service running in the cloud (Power Query Online)
options.B: An automatic flow diagram creator for reports
options.C: A database synchronization service between Azure and AWS
options.D: A workspace migration wizard

explanation: Dataflows run Power Query in the cloud, extracting, transforming, and storing data in Azure Data Lake Storage for reuse across datasets.

text: Where is the output data of a Power BI Dataflow stored?

options.A: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
options.B: Local SQL Server database
options.C: OneDrive for Business
options.D: Directly inside the report pbix file

explanation: Dataflows output data to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 in Common Data Model (CDM) format.

text: What is the benefit of a Shared Dataset in Power BI?

options.A: It allows multiple reports in different workspaces to build off a single master dataset
options.B: It automatically translates report labels into multiple languages
options.C: It removes the limit on the number of daily scheduled refreshes
options.D: It grants edit access to all guest users in Microsoft Entra

explanation: Shared datasets reduce redundancy by letting creators connect reports from different workspaces to a single source of truth.

text: What is the difference between a Dataflow and a Dataset?

options.A: Dataflows handle ETL (Power Query); Datasets hold the loaded data model, relationships, and DAX measures
options.B: Dataflows are for Desktop; Datasets are only for cloud Service
options.C: Datasets can only connect to SQL databases; Dataflows connect to any source
options.D: There is no difference; they are interchangeable

explanation: Dataflows prep and clean data (ETL). Datasets model, establish relationships, define metrics (DAX), and serve report queries.

text: What is a 'Composite Model' in Power BI?

options.A: A model combining DirectQuery sources and Import tables, or multiple DirectQuery sources
options.B: A report combining local Excel files with text files only
options.C: A dataset containing only dynamic measure columns
options.D: A model configured with both Row-Level Security and Object-Level Security

explanation: Composite models allow a report to mix DirectQuery connection to a semantic model with local imports or other database connections.
